## Working Life and Social Policy Index

The **ÇAHSPAR Working Life and Social Policy Index** is an original initiative designed to monitor developments in working life, social policy and social welfare through multidimensional indicators.

It aims to track Türkiye’s working life and social policy landscape regularly by considering job quality, employment, social protection, equality, welfare, sustainability and the future of work together.

## Purpose of the Index

The index’s main purpose is to reveal developments in working life and social policy through **measurable, comparable and trackable indicators**.

Its objectives include:

- Monitoring developments in working life
- Assessing changes in social policy
- Bringing together indicators of workers’ and society’s wellbeing
- Identifying changes over time
- Providing a reliable information source for researchers, decision-makers, public bodies and civil society organisations

## Dimensions of the Index

The methodology will bring together key working life and social policy indicators under several dimensions.

### Working Life
Employment, unemployment, working conditions, wages and key labour market indicators.

### Social Policy
Indicators of social protection, social security, social services and social policy practices.

### Equality and Inclusion
Participation in working life by women, young people and different groups of workers, alongside workplace equality indicators.

### Welfare
Indicators of income, poverty, living conditions and social welfare.

### Sustainability
Sustainable working lives, social sustainability and the future of work.

### The Future of Work
Digital transformation, artificial intelligence, automation, new forms of work and technological change in working life.

## Data Sources

The index is expected to draw on reliable and comparable national and international data sources.

Key sources will include:

**TurkStat (TÜİK) · Social Security Institution (SGK) · Ministry of Labour and Social Security (ÇSGB) · ILO · OECD · Eurostat · World Bank · United Nations**

alongside other relevant institutional data sources.

## Methodology

The methodological framework will cover indicator selection, data standardisation, the construction of dimensions and index calculation.

The methodology, data sources and calculation procedures will be made public so that results are **transparent, traceable and reproducible**.
